_about: Outside facts for the night-sky page (2026-11-18, D16). A row is written to the page only with its url, the source's own words (quote) and the day it was read (read), as scripts/site/pseo/facts.json requires. The Chief's build of 2026-11-17 named the agencies; the Scout fills the rows.

wildlife.name: Great horned owl
wildlife.when: Around sunset ({ss}) and in the hours before sunrise ({sr}).
wildlife.what: Low, far-carrying hoots: hoo, hoo-hoo, hoo, hoo. Courtship calling peaks in November and December.

wildlife.name: Barred owl
wildlife.when: Dusk ({be}) and dawn ({mb}); it also calls by day.
wildlife.what: "Who cooks for you? Who cooks for you?" Loudest in its late-winter courtship.

wildlife.name: Eastern screech-owl
wildlife.what: A descending whinny capped with a trill. Heard most in fall and spring.

wildlife.name: White-tailed deer
wildlife.when: The hour around sunset ({ss}) first, then around sunrise ({sr}).
wildlife.what: Studies find no link between deer activity and the moon's phase; dusk and dawn are the hours, whatever the moon.
wildlife.source: the Chief's build named studies without a citation; the Scout names them

wildlife.name: Coyotes
wildlife.when: Late evening, and around dusk ({be}) and dawn ({mb}).
wildlife.what: Yips and howls carry up the holler. Most vocal in the breeding season, late winter to early spring.
wildlife.source: the Chief's build cited one study on moonlight without naming it; the Scout names it

wildlife.name: Spring peepers and chorus frogs
wildlife.when: After dark, from about {dk}, near the creek.
wildlife.what: A chorus that sounds like sleigh bells from a distance. It starts in February in the counties just north.

wildlife.name: Wild turkey
wildlife.when: Half an hour before sunrise to an hour after.
wildlife.what: Gobbling peaks in late March and early April in the Blue Ridge.

wildlife.name: Blue ghost fireflies
wildlife.when: Between 9:00 and 9:30 PM in spring; 9:30 to 11:00 PM in mid-June.
wildlife.what: A steady blue-green glow low over the forest floor. One record in Lumpkin County so far, so a hope, not a promise.
wildlife.source: Discover Life in America; GBIF records

wildlife.name: Fireflies
wildlife.when: From dusk to full dark: {be} to {dk}.
wildlife.what: They start low to the ground and rise into the trees as it darkens. Few flash on clear full-moon nights, and bright lights put them off.

wildlife.name: Whip-poor-will
wildlife.when: All night, most at dusk and dawn.
wildlife.what: Its own name, over and over. It calls more when the moon is over half lit and above the horizon.

wildlife.name: Katydids
wildlife.what: The summer night chorus is katydids and crickets, from late June until frost.

wildlife.name: Bats
wildlife.when: Around dusk, about {be}, on nights above 50 degrees.
wildlife.what: They leave their day roosts at dusk to hunt moths and mosquitoes over the creek.

wildlife.name: Black bear
wildlife.what: Present in the North Georgia mountains. Most den between November and January and are out again by early April.
wildlife.source: Georgia DNR; NC Wildlife; PA Game Commission

wildlife.name: Pileated woodpecker
wildlife.what: Loud drumming and a ringing cuk-cuk-cuk that rises and falls.

showers.name: The Geminids
showers.line: The best shower of the year, all evening

showers.name: The Ursids
showers.line: A quiet shower on the longest night

showers.name: Christmas Eve
showers.line: A near-full moon over the Christmas stay
showers.source: the sky table itself (no outside fact)

showers.name: The Quadrantids
showers.line: A short, sharp shower before dawn
